    Initial background planes
    
  
    Apply the stored parent and child writes to two 64×64 tile planes. The initial
  fill and layer order are chosen here; live updates, camera, palette effects and
  other scene layers are not reproduced. When marked, missing tiles are magenta
  and missing palette banks are cyan.
    
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
    Animate linked transfers

    Object animations and static layouts
    
  
    Browse indexed and compact object lists, sequences and static layouts. Graphics and palettes are chosen
  manually; their pairing with a sequence is not inferred. The preview uses
  1D tiles and a chosen tick rate, treating zero duration as one preview tick.
  Layered sequences can be overlaid at a shared origin using duration plus one
  preview tick per frame. Their live offsets, task state and clock are not
  reproduced. Constructor phases use their stored counter thresholds, starting
  the 8-bit counter at zero for the preview. Affine, mosaic and special object
  modes are shown as outlines only.

  Moving markers use linear interpolation for inspection; they do not reconstruct the original interpolation,

  not a proved live selection range.

    Tilemap and rectangle explorer
    
  
    Choose extracted cells and optionally interpret them as 4-bit background
  tile entries. Graphics, tile placement and colors are selected manually;
  the preview does not establish the game's actual scene or palette pairing.
  Localized transfer rectangles retain four source rows of 24 halfwords; the
  original destination row stride is 64 bytes.
  Type-2 source rectangles can contain color words; interpreting them as tile
  entries is a manual preview.
  You can apply one selected color bank to every cell, or use the stored
  palette IDs within the selected palette source.
    
  
    The nine fixed-width maps come from the original
  copier's verified source rectangles; two localized callers share one map.
  Graphics and palette choices are manual and do not identify the original screen.
    
  
    This 30×20 source is copied into a destination with a 32-cell row pitch.
  The graphics and color choices follow the loader and its preceding initializer. Color-zero transparency
  and other layers are not composited; later palette changes, blending and the screen's identity remain unverified.
    
  
  
  
    Each rectangle has a two-byte height/width header;
  its 15×16 halfword cells follow. The original task was verified copying row zero;
  the shared helper was checked separately for the remaining rows.
    
  
    Each rectangle starts with its height and width in bytes, followed by
  its 16-bit cells. Two linked grids come from the type-2 transfers when that source is available.
    
  
    Three direct maps are selected by the language-byte
  branch; the others are selected through the directories. The caller controls
  the tile addend, graphics and palette. These previews do not identify a scene.
    
  
    The five maps are physical source rectangles.
  The live-height map's 16 available rows are an inspection bound, not a claim
  about the original task's live row count.
    
  
    These three stored matrices provide two language-dependent 26×7 layouts and four 18-cell initialization rows.
    
  
  
    
    
    
  
    
  
    
    
    
    The copier adds this value to each stored halfword with 16-bit wrapping;
    87 was used in the controlled reader check. Set 0 to inspect stored cells.
    
    
    
    
    
  
    
  
    
    
    
    The staged view adds two zero columns to the second template. These
    transformations use 16-bit wrapping; graphics and palette selection remain manual.
    
  
    
  
    
    
    Firaga sequence timing is not established; the chosen rate is only for preview.
    The packed flags and second byte are displayed as stored.

      Progression and pricing records
      
  
      These European tables retain physical IDs and stored values. They do not
  establish a character's live state, reward availability, skill names, item
  links or the result of running the original game code.
      
  
      Progression deltas and discount
    
      Eight stored deltas feed corresponding progress slots; the discount byte
    is used by a separate price reader. The final byte remains unclassified.
      
    
      
  
      
  
      Progression requirements
    
      The original reader checks all eight minima for each unreceived physical
    row. The returned halfword and output byte are shown without inferring an
    item or reward identity; a zero return can still belong to a matching row.
      
    
      
  
      
  
      Progression selection conditions
    
      All three minima must pass. If any of the eight slot minima is nonzero,
    at least one active minimum must pass; a nonzero flag is checked separately.
    The first eligible physical row is significant. A row without conditions
    stores zero; an exhausted table leaves the previous value unchanged.
      
    
      
  
      
  
      Trade price parameters
    
      Count zero reads byte 0x41, the high byte of the markup field. Counts
    1–30 use the following discount bytes. The preceding 64 bytes are preserved
    as unclassified data; live flags and other price inputs are not simulated.

      Song track sequences
      
  
      Explore one track or play the extracted tracks together. Known PCM and
  CGB wave instruments can use extracted samples; CGB square voices use their
  stored duty cycles. Fixed-rate PCM uses an assumed mixer rate that can be
  changed below; the default was observed in one European checkpoint. Other
  voices fall back to sine waves. Tempo commands from all tracks can guide the
  timing even when listening to one track. Frame timing models the driver's
  nominal frame cadence and starts at one tick per frame; the continuous
  estimate uses the manual rate before the first tempo command. Disabling song
  tempo uses the manual rate throughout. The live tempo multiplier, mixing,
  bends, envelopes and effects remain approximate. The trace has safety limits.

      Text reader registry
      
  
      These are stored callback slots. A link identifies an extracted archive whose
  reader address matches the callback; it does not establish that the callback
  was executed or describe when the game uses it.

      Browse archive programs by reader and language. Commands and operands are
  labeled as stored; dynamic substitutions and formatting are not executed.
  Hidden commands leave a space. Normal font uses a visually matched European
  Latin subset; other glyphs retain their original image. Program labels show a
  short recognized preview; � marks unknown glyphs.

  are not simulated. Shared programs and header or fill targets remain distinct.

      Select a sprite to preview its frames.
      
  
      Playback starts at the selected frame and continues to the end, or repeats
  when looping is enabled. Stored durations use the chosen preview rate; a zero
  duration is shown for one preview tick. This is not game timing.
      
  
      
  
  
      
  
  
  
  
      
  

      

      
  
      Actor, equipment and script sprite sequences
      
  
      Browse extracted battle, equipment and script sprite bindings and preview
  their stored frames. Script witnesses describe conditional source relationships,
  not guaranteed live actor behavior. Palette selection is manual. The preview uses a chosen
  tick rate; task commands, game timing, live palettes and composition of actor
  parts are not reproduced. Shared index roots are not sequence headers.
      
  
  
  
  
      These sequences are identified by source offset and index cell. Actor, facing and scene assignments depend on live conditions.
